reply.text:
Here you go — one tiny file, two inputs to run against it.

```python
def show(items):
    for i in range(len(items) - 1):
        print(items[i])


# Example input 1
show(["a", "b", "c"])

# Example input 2
show(["x"])
```

The intent is obviously "print every item in `items`". Run it and see what actually comes out — and notice that input 2 is where it goes quiet.

Two things to keep in mind while you fix it:

- `range(len(items) - 1)` produces the indices `0 .. len(items)-2`, so the **last** index is never in the loop at all.
- The reason it fails "nearly every time" rather than always: on a one-element list `len(items) - 1` is `0`, so the loop body never runs and the output is empty — the same bug wearing a different mask.
